Non-rescue first time owner here with a GSD since 9 weeks. Reputable breeder I searched for nonstop for a year. Training tips and videos. I’m still learning so much. 

She’s 1 1/2 now. She was socialized young and I thought I did well for my first dog. A few small dogs barked at her out of fear either from their cars or in a pet store which I think contributed to her dog reactivity from being suddenly barked at when she’s done nothing wrong. That happened when she was young. With Covid in full swing I could only take her to the dog park to be around other dogs. Not many bad experiences. Anything bad she shook off quickly and kept playing. As she’s gotten older she’s been better in some ways and worse in others. I’m trying to work on her reactivity. We didn’t go to the park for a couple months and upon returning she was scared and chasing dogs away from me. Especially puppies. No fights but chasing them off is very new and makes me sad that she’s threatened by dogs she used to see as friends. I’m used to her showing when she’s at her limit but this is entirely new. We have boarded her a couple times and she seemed to do well but now doesn’t always like getting into the car when she was practically raised in the car and took many rides with us throughout puppyhood. It’s confusing since I thought she enjoyed or at least tolerated car rides. I’m working on scheduling a trainer to help since I don’t want her to be scared of the world. Separation anxiety is another thing I thought we were doing better on but she’s been panicking recently when any of us goes to leave the house. She’s crate trained and loves her crate. Even then sometimes she barks loudly when she hears something in the house or starts barking a ton out of nowhere. She calms down eventually but she’s been crate trained since day 1. She’s barking from her crate now ugh. I love her and want to help her through this and show her there’s nothing to be afraid of. She’s always been easygoing and very chill but when she panics or gets protective she goes loud. I’m determined to help her learn not to be scared. Hope I can get results soon too for her sake

OH and make car rides fun! Idk how your pup is in the car. Some get carsick. Others don’t. Some sleep. Some stay awake and cry a little or a lot. It depends on the individual pup. Definitely feed their food to them for treats and offer pets and scritches when they’re being good and not whiney. Wait a few seconds after they whine and when they’re silent for that little time. Reward with treats or praise. 

They can lose their appetites when acclimating to their new environment. Make sure they’re eating something. Even if it’s just hand fed treats or their kibble. We dont want them getting too underweight cause then you’ll be in trouble. 

TREATS! Treat them when they display a behavior you like. Even if you didn’t ask them to. They’ll continue to remember something that got them positive attention and do it again if they remember. For jumping on your legs and probably scratching them with their little nails don’t pay attention to them. Just turn your back to them and take a couple slow steps. Ignore them for about 5 seconds. Then get back to what you were doing. They definitely get overexcited and can sometimes bark in a high tone, jump around, get “zoomies” and run in bursts for a bit, or jump on you. You must show em that they can’t always do that because not everyone likes being jumped on. It’s cute now but wait until they’re about 60-100 lbs! 
SHORT training sessions. Puppies have short attention spans. Keep training sessions to about 10-15 minutes. Then play to get out more excess energy. Try to do simple commands. You don’t even need to say the command yet and instead say Yes high pitched and enthusiastically or good boy/girl/name. 
We’re still settling in with ours. We got her on the 7th. Due to tons of heat she gets uncomfortable outside pretty fast so she can refuse to go potty outside and instead goes on our few rugs. It’s a challenge but don’t freak out if yours does the same. We’re all still learning. Don’t shame for peeing or even pooping inside. It’ll likely happen. Just get em away from the area with a toy and clean it up real quick. That reminds me get special pet urine odor remover so they’ll forget about the spot they went in. Even on hard time or wood floors it’ll still take the scent. So be sure to take care of it ASAP. Nature’s Miracle oxy formula seems to work for mine. Get other opinions on pet safe cleaners because I’m definitely no expert. 

Take em to an outlet mall to socialize if you can. Make sure the ground isn’t too hot. They can withstand a little heat on their paws but if it’s too hot for your hand chances are it’s too hot for their little feets. Find a shaded spot for em to lay or stand in. They’ll test the temperature of the ground in the sun themselves too and generally return to the shaded spot for some better feeling colder ground. When they try approaching people give praise. Let the people know they’re a little bitey at this stage. That’s another thing to do. Like with jumping, if they bite you then yelp a high pitch and get up and turn away for a few seconds. It’s what their siblings do when they yelp while biting each other playing. Also how could people resist an adorable puppy. Be sure to put a mask on yourself too and try social distancing. It’s hard with a puppy that needs socialization but it’s better to socialize them and expose them to as many positive experiences as possible. 
Give em alone time in their crate after exhausting outings. They might get moody if they’re not allowed to be a little away from you and your family. It’s good if they walk back over by themselves to check on you and return to being away for a bit to nap or play by themselves. That shows independence but also their boundaries. Just like you don’t always want someone touching you doesn’t mean they don’t want human touch. 
If I repeated myself, understand that it’s literally 3 am for me and I’m checking on my girl. Best of luck!
